messages:
alex: Heads-up — ALB started evicting a bunch of edge targets in us-west-2 around 17:31 UTC. Targets went UNHEALTHY almost simultaneously, readiness probes failing. Any obvious suspects?

maria: Looking at metrics now. SNAT allocation usage spiked hard at the same time (almost full). CloudWatch shows ephemeral ports used ~2500/2550 for the nodes serving the edge pool.

kevin: That'll do it. If ephemeral ports are exhausted, new outbound connections from pods (including replies to ALB healthchecks or kubelet probes that require outbound allocations) will fail — leading to timeouts and ALB target deregistration.

tara: Quick question — ALB healthchecks connect to pod IP:port from the ALB nodes, so why do pods need ephemeral outbound ports for that?

kevin: Good nuance — usually not. But our edge stack has sidecars (envoy) that perform egress or local routing; some healthchecks trigger proxy paths or egress NAT for certain subnets, which need source ports. Also kubelet liveness/readiness checks from host can create patterns that touch conntrack entries. Combined bursts from CI/canary traffic + control plane probes can exhaust the ephemeral pool.

alex: Found an accept() failure in the sidecar logs: "accept() failed: EADDRNOTAVAIL" repeated a few times during the window. Envoy logs also show a lot of 504s.

maria: Paste of CloudWatch snippet (abridged):
```
snat_allocations: 98% used -> 2500/2550
conntrack_established: 45k -> 190k
node_count: unchanged
pod_restarts: +3 (same window)
```

kevin: Short-term mitigation suggestions: scale up nodepool serving that AZ, bump conntrack and ephemeral port range, and consider enabling port reuse sysctls. We should also throttle the CI job that saturated egress.

maria: Performed quick mitigations: scaled nodepool + bumped sysctls on affected nodes: 
```
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="10240 61000"
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
```
I also adjusted the NAT gateway connection tracking timeout for TCP to be slightly lower for ephemeral entries.

tara: For longer-term: add jitter to readiness probes and increase failureThreshold so brief port pressure doesn't evict healthy pods. Example proposal for the edge deployment: readinessProbe: periodSeconds: 5, failureThreshold: 6, initialDelaySeconds: 10. Also add a rollout with canary 10%.

alex: Agree. I'll roll a canary with the probe changes + the nodepool size bump held for 30m to validate. I'll also coordinate with infra CI owners to rate-limit that job.

sre-bot: ALERT: ALB target group tg-xyz health check failure rate >5% for 3m (https://console.aws/xyz) :rotating_light:

maria: After scaling + sysctl tweaks, SNAT usage dropped back to ~20% and targets are re-registering. We'll keep the scaling for another hour to ensure stability.

kevin: Postmortem action items: (1) instrument ephemeral port usage per-node + alert at 70%, (2) add probe jitter/backoff to edge deployments, (3) validate sidecar egress paths to avoid unnecessary SNAT, (4) add runbook steps for rapid nodepool scaling.

tara: +1 on the runbook. I'll draft a short playbook with commands and quick checks.

alex: Thanks all — following up with a short incident note and action items. :thumbsup:
